metadata.title: Creative learning environments and mathematics self-efficacy as predictors of mathematics achievement: Insights from PISA 2022 across three countries – Korea, Canada, and Türkiye

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 microdata for mathematics, restricting the analysis to three countries (Korea, Canada, Türkiye) and modeling latent constructs (creative learning environments and mathematics self-efficacy) with mathematics achievement as the outcome. The manuscript does not report the use of PISA sampling/student weights or any replicate-weight procedure; therefore, it is unclear whether complex survey design was incorporated into estimation. Mathematics achievement is handled via PISA plausible values (PV1MATH–PV10MATH), with analyses performed across the ten PVs, which is the standard approach for PISA achievement scaling. Missing data were addressed using regression-based imputation and FIML, but the paper does not specify whether weighting was applied in either approach.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2022 mathematics-focused data for 15-year-old students in Korea, Canada, and Türkiye. The analytic sample corresponds to the participating-student counts reported in Table 1 (Korea: 6454; Canada: 23073; Türkiye: 7250). The study then constructs indices from questionnaire items (ST335 for creative school/class environment; ST336 for creative peers/family environment; ST291 for mathematics self-efficacy) and models mathematics achievement using PISA mathematics plausible values (PV1MATH–PV10MATH). Missing data were handled via regression-based imputation and FIML estimation, with robustness checks across these approaches.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Structural equation model path coefficients (bootstrap 95% CI): Korea CREATFAM→MATHEF21 β=0.208 (p<0.001); Korea CREATSCH→MATHEF21 β=0.160 (p<0.001). Canada CREATFAM→MATHEF21 β=0.171 (p<0.001); Canada CREATSCH→MATHEF21 β=0.293 (p<0.001). Türkiye CREATFAM→MATHEF21 β=0.179 (p<0.001); Türkiye CREATSCH→MATHEF21 β=0.247 (p<0.001). Variance explained: MATHEF21 %11 (Korea), %17 (Canada), %14 (Türkiye).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics the study leveraged Creative peers and family environment and Creative school and class environment to predict Mathematics self-efficacy (MATHEF21), finding that both creative learning environments had positive, statistically significant effects on MATHEF21 in Korea, Canada, and Türkiye. This indicates that strengthening creativity-supportive peer/family and school/class practices may raise students’ mathematics confidence, which is a key proximal factor for later achievement, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Structural equation model path coefficients (bootstrap 95% CI): MATHEF21→MATHACH β=0.521 (Korea, p<0.001), β=0.505 (Canada, p<0.001), β=0.314 (Türkiye, p<0.001). Direct effects: CREATFAM→MATHACH β=0.034 (Korea, p<0.05), β=0.036 (Canada, p<0.001), β=0.078 (Türkiye, p<0.001). CREATSCH→MATHACH β=-0.103 (Korea, p<0.001), β=-0.143 (Canada, p<0.001), β=-0.148 (Türkiye, p<0.001). Indirect effects via MATHEF21: CREATFAM→MATHEF21→MATHACH β=0.109 (Korea), β=0.086 (Canada), β=0.056 (Türkiye); CREATSCH→MATHEF21→MATHACH β=0.083 (Korea), β=0.148 (Canada), β=0.077 (Türkiye). Variance explained: MATHACH %26 (Korea), %22 (Canada), %10 (Türkiye).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 Mathematics the study leveraged Mathematics self-efficacy (MATHEF21), Creative peers and family environment, and Creative school and class environment to predict Mathematics achievement (MATHACH; PV1MATH–PV10MATH), finding that MATHEF21 had a consistent positive effect while creative peers/family showed small positive direct effects and creative school/class showed small negative direct effects. This indicates that creativity-supportive environments may improve achievement primarily by boosting mathematics self-efficacy (indirect pathway), and that classroom creativity practices may need alignment with mathematics learning demands to avoid unintended negative associations, though causality cannot be inferred from cross-sectional SEM.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2022 mathematics data for 15-year-old students in Korea (n=6454), Canada (n=23073), and Türkiye (n=7250) to test a structural equation model linking creative learning environments to mathematics achievement through mathematics self-efficacy (MATHEF21). Mathematics achievement is modeled using PISA plausible values PV1MATH–PV10MATH, and the authors report path coefficients with bootstrap confidence intervals. The model shows that both creative peers/family and creative school/class environments positively predict MATHEF21 across all three countries, with MATHEF21 explaining a moderate share of achievement variance (MATHEF21→MATHACH β≈0.31–0.52). For achievement, creative peers/family has small positive direct effects, while creative school/class has small negative direct effects, but both creative environments have positive indirect effects via MATHEF21. Limitations include the cross-sectional design (associational not causal) and unclear use of PISA sampling weights/replicate weights.
